subject: Post-call: FinCommerce concurrency & rate-limit qualification
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Lee <ethan.lee@fincommerce.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 22:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: concurrency targets, streaming needs, and next steps

Thanks again for taking time today — good conversation. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size a short PoC and pull together a firm ratecard for you:

Summary of what we heard (please flag anything I got wrong):
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 350ms for single-turn prompts at 512 tokens.
- Sustained throughput: ~120 reqs/sec during business hours, with expected peaks up to 400 reqs/sec for a 90s burst window (checkout events).
- Concurrent open-streaming sessions: up to 150 active streams (these are streaming chat sessions where we push incremental tokens).
- Connection model: your frontend plans to reuse WebSocket connections (1 per user-device), multiplexing multiple requests per connection for a subset of flows.

Questions / asks for sizing:
1) Can you upload a 24‑hour sample traffic file (requests per second, typical payload sizes, % streaming vs non-streaming)? I attached a template — you can also just reply with CSV.
2) Are there strict per-tenant quotas (each merchant) or is this pooled across your account?
3) Any hard SLAs for tail latency under burst (p99/P99.9)?

Proposed Redwood configuration (preliminary):
- Connection pooling: reuse + multiplexing; recommend connectionKeepAlive with 30s idle and maximum 8 concurrent multiplexed requests per connection for the checkout flows.
- Concurrency model: reserve a dedicated capacity pool sized for 220 concurrent model contexts with auto-burst to shared pool up to 400 during peaks.
- Rate limits: soft per-account qps gate at 250r/s with a burst window allowance up to 400r/s for up to 120s (configurable).

Next steps:
- Ethan: share traffic sample and confirm per-merchant quota behavior.
- FinCommerce procurement: we’ll follow with an initial ratecard + PoC order form once traffic is confirmed.
- Ben: I’ve looped you for a short design doc and a recommended Redwood instance config for the PoC.

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-conn-matrix.pdf (draft), PoC traffic template (fincommerce-traffic-sample.csv).

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0243

Redwood Inference — predictable inference, production scale

From: Ethan Lee <ethan.lee@fincommerce.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@fincommerce.io>, FinCommerce Procurement <procurement@fincommerce.io>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: concurrency targets, streaming needs, and next steps

Thanks Neha — this is great and mostly aligns. A few clarifications: 

- The 400 reqs/sec peak is per-account (we run multi-tenant merchants; top 10 merchants account for ~80% of peak). We will likely want per-merchant throttles to avoid noisy-neighbor behavior.
- Streaming sessions: 150 active streams is our estimate for peak; those streams emit small tokens frequently (avg 15 tokens/sec).
- Tail SLA: we need p99 < 800ms (hard) during burst windows; p99.9 is nice-to-have but not required for Phase 1.

I uploaded the 24h sample to the drive link (same link as you included) — file is "fincommerce-traffic-sample.csv". It has per-minute bins, and a merchant_id column.

Procurement (cc): we’d like a 60-day PoC with telemetry access and a short-term discount to run verification against our peak patterns. Who should procurement expect the PoC order form from?

—Ethan

Appreciate the sample, Ethan — I pulled a quick profile off the CSV and added a couple of notes inline. High-level thoughts from an infra/SE perspective:

- Multiplexing: your approach (1 WS per device, up to 8 concurrent streams per connection) is good. For checkout flows where you expect bursts, keep multiplex limit lower (4) to prioritize fast handshake and reduce head-of-line blocking.
- KV cache sizing: for chat-like interactions with streaming, we should reserve for ~300MB KV per model instance; we can compress tokens on hot paths to reduce memory pressure.
- Burst model: we can configure a temporary elastic burst pool that ramps to shared capacity within 10s and scales down over 150s to avoid oscillation. This matches your 90–120s burst window.

Proposed practical rate limits for PoC (recommended):
1) Per-merchant soft QPS: 200 r/s
2) Global account QPS: 350 r/s with an enforced 120s burst window up to 450 r/s for safety
3) Concurrent open streams: cap 170 overall, with prioritization for top-tier merchants during burst via token bucket weights

I’ll draft a PoC config (instance sizes, connection-pool settings, autoscale policy) and attach by EOD. If procurement needs a formal order, Neha — I can route the ratecard + PoC sheet to procurement and include a templated SOW.

Ben

Hi Neha / Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary. Procurement is ready to review a PoC order form and the draft ratecard. A couple of items on our side: 
- We need an explicit clause for per-merchant QoS (no single merchant should cause >20% degradation to others).
- Billing: can we get line items for reserved capacity vs overage/burst usage for the PoC period?
- Data handling: please include a short note on session data retention and whether logs contain payloads (we prefer redaction for PII).

If you can send a one-page PoC order + ratecard and SOW, we’ll circulate internally and aim to return counters within 7 business days.

Regards,
Aisha Patel
Head of Procurement, FinCommerce
